answer: Resist sybils with latency triangulation: each epoch, beacons on different continents send time-locked cipher challenges that an identity must answer within milliseconds, and the round-trip times pin its network location to one vertex of the map. A lone agent answers from its own corner like a comet streaking past one beacon, but a farmer's thousand clones all share one machine and one path, so their timings collapse into a single point. Cloning names is free; cloning distinct, fast network locations is not.
